reason: Alert 1 alert-TP: endpoint = param (user input) flows directly to URL construction at sink line 28. The isNonPublicAddress check validates the resolved IP but does not prevent SSRF since attacker-controlled hostnames can resolve to public IPs. The separate DNS resolution followed by fetch using original endpoint allows classic SSRF exploits.

evidence.note: User param assigned to endpoint, DNS resolved separately, then fetch uses original endpoint - classic SSRF pattern
